_strings.@@1f3f9456bc7d: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW for 2025 — advance Child Tax Credit payments must be RECONCILED on the return: a taxpayer who elected advance payments of their 2025 Child Tax Credit on the 2024 return MUST file a 2025 return to reconcile them, even if not otherwise required to file (and even if Minnesota-source income is below $14,950). The repayment of advance Child Tax Credit payments is computed on the new Schedule M1CWFC line 27 and reported on the new Form M1 line 14b. The advance-payment election itself now covers the 2026 credit (paper filers who elect mail to Mail Station 0015 instead of 0010). Resolve via: 2025 Schedule M1CWFC line 27 and the Form M1 line 14b instructions (the citation URL); the advance payments actually received come from the MN DOR, and calc.state_tax adds no line 14 amounts.
_strings.@@228cbf697124: Treaty conformity — MN conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MN income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MN return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Minnesota's resident return (Form M1) starts from federal adjusted gross income: the 2025 M1 instructions for Line 1 state "Line 1—Federal Adjusted Gross Income. Enter your 2025 federal adjusted gross income from line 11a of Form 1040 or 1040-SR, or 1040-NR." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through. The Minnesota additions (M1 line 2 = Schedule M1M line 10 and Schedule M1MB line 9) contain NO line that adds back income exempt under a U.S. income tax treaty. The only treaty references in the 2025 M1 instructions are FAVORABLE to the taxpayer (a nonresident alien may claim the standard deduction if allowed by a U.S. income tax treaty — stated in the What's new standard-deduction section, in the Line 4 itemized-deduction paragraph, and in the Standard Deduction Table for Line 4 note). Because there is no treaty addback, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> conforms.

_strings.@@37965bb69803: Renter's Credit — Minnesota residents who paid rent in 2025 on a building where property taxes were payable for 2025 (or payments in lieu of property taxes were payable in 2025) and who received a Certificate of Rent Paid (CRP). A copy of any CRP used to claim the credit must be provided with the return.

_strings.@@98ff5ee6b61f: Minnesota Child and Dependent Care Credit — MN taxpayers who paid someone (other than a dependent child or stepchild younger than 19) to care for a qualifying person while you (and your spouse if filing jointly) were working or looking for work — qualifying person and expenses are the same as for the federal child and dependent care credit. Also available to licensed family daycare operators caring for their own dependent child under age six, and for a child born in 2025 if you did not participate in a pre-tax dependent care assistance program. Refundable, unlike the federal credit.

ITIN may be used if no SSN. You may ELECT to receive advance payments of your 2026 Child Tax Credit on Schedule M1CWFC (you must be eligible for a 2025 Child Tax Credit to receive 2026 advance payments; paper filers who elect mail to Mail Station 0015 instead of 0010). _strings.@@fae971a8cc50: K-12 Education Credit — MN parents/guardians who paid education-related expenses in 2025 for a qualifying child in grades K-12 (a qualifying child is the same as for the federal Earned Income Credit). Qualifying expenses include tutoring by a qualified instructor, instructional materials, music lessons, and certain educational services (private school tuition does NOT qualify for the credit — it is a Schedule M1M subtraction only). Refundable.
_strings.@@fc302c3d9b72: Minnesota Working Family Credit (state Earned Income Tax Credit) — Full-year or part-year MN residents who earned income from a job or self-employment, were self-employed, or have qualifying children (qualifying children and qualifying older children determined on Schedule M1DQC). Combined with the Child Tax Credit on Schedule M1CWFC. ITINs may be used if you, your spouse, or your qualifying children have no SSN. Part-year residents qualify based on their percentage of income assignable to Minnesota.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form M1 line 10: "Tax from the table or schedules in the Form M1 instructions". Instructions, Line 10 — Tax From Table: "Turn to the tax table on pages 32 through 38. Using the amount on line 9, find the tax amount in the column under your filing status." Tax Rate Schedules, p.39: "You must use these schedules if line 9 of Form M1 is $86,800 or more... If line 9 of Form M1 is less than $86,800, you must use the tax table on pages 32 through 38." This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form M1 line 1 = federal adjusted gross income (2025 federal Form 1040/1040-SR line 11a, or 1040-NR), adjusted for Minnesota items if any apply: ADD M1 line 2 additions (Schedule M1M line 10 and Schedule M1MB line 9) and SUBTRACT M1 line 6 (state income tax refund from federal Schedule 1 line 1) and M1 line 7 subtractions (Schedule M1M line 40 and Schedule M1MB line 22 — renumbered for 2025 from 2024's M1M line 35 / M1MB line 21). The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (M1 line 4) and $5,200 per dependent (M1 line 5) to reach M1 line 9, Minnesota taxable income, to which the rate schedule applies. Pass exemptions_count = 0 (Minnesota has no taxpayer/spouse personal exemption) and dependents_count = number of dependents claimed on Schedule M1DQC. Adjudication note (two-pass, 2025): the 2025 schedules were drafted from the M1 booklet's p.39 Tax Rate Schedules and re-verified digit-by-digit against the DOR's Dec 16, 2024 indexing press release, the Tax Year 2025 Tax Professional Desk Reference Chart, AND the DOR 'Income Tax Rates and Brackets' web page — all four agree on every boundary (single 32,570/106,990/198,630; MFJ 47,620/189,180/330,410; MFS 23,810/94,590/165,205 — exactly half of MFJ; HoH 40,100/161,130/264,050), the four rates (5.35%/6.80%/7.85%/9.85%, unchanged since 2023), the standard deduction ($14,950/$29,900/$14,950/$22,500), and the $5,200 dependent exemption. 2025 indexing factor: +2.886% from tax year 2024, rounded to the nearest $10. CRITICAL — the TAX TABLE MANDATE THRESHOLD MOVED for 2025: it is $86,800, NOT 2024's $90,000. 'If line 9 of Form M1 is less than $86,800, you must use the tax table on pages 32 through 38' and 'You must use these schedules if line 9 of Form M1 is $86,800 or more' (2025 M1 instructions, p.39); the printed table's last row reads '86,800 & over: Use tax rate schedules on page 39.' The table is built on $100-band midpoints chained from the printed schedule constants, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands — the filed form must use the table below $86,800. (Spot-checked: table row $79,600-$79,700 prints 4,944 / 4,726 / 5,071 / 4,835 for Single/MFJ/MFS/HoH — all four equal midpoint bracket math at $79,650.) Qualifying Surviving Spouse: the p.39 rate-schedule column is titled 'Married filing jointly or qualifying widow(er)' — QSS uses the MFJ schedule exactly as mapped here, and the QSS standard deduction ($29,900 with 0 age/blind boxes) equals MFJ. Minnesota has NO personal exemption for the taxpayer or spouse: Form M1 line 5 is for DEPENDENTS only ($5,200 per dependent from Schedule M1DQC; the Tax Year 2025 Desk Reference Chart prints the Minnesota personal exemption as $0). Callers must pass exemptions_count = 0 and put dependents in dependents_count. Dependent-exemption phase-out NOT modeled (Worksheet for Line 5, 2025 thresholds re-indexed): the $5,200-per-dependent total is reduced by 2% for each $2,500 ($1,250 MFS) that M1 line 1 AGI exceeds $239,050 Single / $298,800 Head of Household / $358,550 MFJ-or-Surviving-Spouse / $179,275 MFS, and is $0 once the excess is more than $122,500 ($61,250 MFS). Standard-deduction limitation NOT modeled (Worksheets A & B for Line 4, 2025 thresholds re-indexed): if M1 line 1 AGI exceeds $238,950 ($119,475 MFS), the deduction is reduced by the LESSER of 80% of the deduction or [3% of the excess over $238,950/$119,475 (capped: enter $91,350, or $45,675 MFS, if AGI exceeds $330,300/$165,150) + 10% of the excess over $330,300 ($165,150 MFS)]; if AGI is $1,083,150 or more, the deduction is reduced by 80% (Worksheet B). Additional standard deduction for age 65+/blind NOT modeled, and the 2025 amounts CHANGED (Standard Deduction Table for Line 4): +$2,000 per checked box for Single and Head of Household (up to 2 boxes; 2024 was $1,950); +$1,550 per checked box for Married Filing Jointly (up to 4), Married Filing Separately (up to 4), and Qualified Surviving Spouse (up to 2) — unchanged at $1,550. Born before January 2, 1961 counts as 65 or older for 2025. Enter it on the form's line 4. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled: Married Filing Separately gets NO standard deduction if the spouse claims itemized deductions ('Not allowed' row); nonresident aliens may claim it only if allowed by a U.S. income tax treaty; the deduction is also disallowed for a return covering less than twelve months due to a change in the annual accounting period; a filer claimable as another's dependent uses the Worksheet for Line 4 - Dependent Standard Deduction (greater of $1,250 or earned income + $350, capped at $14,950, plus $2,000/$1,550 age/blind additions) — itemizers use Schedule M1SA instead. Printed rate-schedule constants check (2025): every '$X +' constant equals the exact cumulative sum of the prior brackets rounded to the cent (single 1,742.50/6,803.06/13,996.80 vs exact 1,742.495/6,803.055/13,996.795; MFJ 2,547.67/12,173.75/23,260.31 vs exact 2,547.67/12,173.75/23,260.305; HoH 2,145.35/10,375.39/18,454.61 all exact; MFS 1,273.84/6,086.88 vs exact 1,273.835/6,086.875), EXCEPT the MFS top-bracket constant $11,630.16, which chains the rounded prior constant (exact marginal math gives $11,630.1525). Maximum divergence from pure marginal math: $0.01. NOT modeled — amounts added after line 10: Minnesota Alternative Minimum Tax (Schedule M1MT, M1 line 11; can apply even without federal AMT); M1 line 14a other taxes (Schedule M1HOME first-time-homebuyer recapture, Schedule M1529 education-savings-account recapture, Schedule M1LS tax on lump-sum distributions, and the Net Investment Income Tax on individuals with net investment income over $1,000,000 — Schedule NIIT, unchanged for 2025 and now reported on line 14a); and NEW for 2025 M1 line 14b, repayment of advance Child Tax Credit payments (Schedule M1CWFC line 27), which a filer who elected 2025 advance payments on the 2024 return must report. Part-year residents and nonresidents: tax is prorated by the Minnesota-source percentage on Schedule M1NR (2025 M1NR lines 28 and 29 -> M1 lines 13a/13b) — NOT modeled; this pack computes full-year-resident tax. M1 line 9 (Minnesota taxable income) = line 3 (federal AGI + line 2 additions) - line 4 (standard/itemized deduction) - line 5 (dependent exemptions) - line 6 (taxable state income tax refund) - line 7 (M1M/M1MB subtractions). If additions, subtractions, or a taxable state refund apply, adjust the supplied taxable_base per the base guidance. The form says 'If zero or less, leave blank' — the engine's max(0, ...) floor matches. Rounding: the M1 instructions say 'Round the dollar amounts to the nearest dollar. For example: 129.49 becomes 129, and 129.50 becomes 130' (Getting Started) — the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches, and vector 1 below is the exact .50 half-up tie.
